title: Phase 1 walking skeleton design on Claude Code
prompt: Let's focus on Claude Code for now and make sure to revisit Copilot CLI and VS Code later today.
summary: One Rust binary (hook client + core + CLI); prompts and Stop only; derived budgets; spikes S1-S4 before ship.
rationale: Claude Code is the only surface with a proven card path; Windows laptop test showed the card renders under the reply and Python hooks are too slow, so the client is compiled. Imran chose Windows first, Linux in CI.

title: Encryption at rest deferred for Phase 1
prompt: Let's defer encryption - we can revisit later whether we even require it
summary: Plain SQLite in a user-only file; no SQLCipher, no keychain. ADR-0002/0003 flagged; accepted risk in threat model.
rationale: Owner decision (Imran, 2026-10-31); removes Windows Perl build friction and key management until the need is confirmed.

title: Claude Code Stop hook budget raised to 100 ms p95
prompt: Chose "Raise to 100 ms at p95" on the decision card "Set the hook speed limit after the laptop missed 50 ms at p95?"
summary: Whole-process p95 budget for the synchronous Stop hook is 100 ms (was 50 ms). e2e default 100 ms, Windows CI stays 200 ms, install self-test reports against 100 ms. ADR-0005, architecture and coaching-loop spec flagged review-suggested.
rationale: Laptop measured p50 27.5 ms, p95 66.8-70.5 ms whole process; in-process p95 3.1 ms. The gap is Windows process start.

title: Rung judge for Claude uses the person's own claude -p; API key becomes fallback

rationale: Imran: AIQ is first-party to the user who installs it; terms page allows an end user to sign in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription. Tension with the 'route requests through plan credentials on behalf of users' sentence recorded; review owed before distribution.

title: Copilot CLI tips render in Copilot CLI's status line
